window: GA4 daily series finalised through 15 Aug (16 Aug broken-read, within T-2 reprocessing window — see TASK-02) + 7d snapshot 27 Jul–2 Aug · Clarity finalised through 15 Aug · Shopify abandoned-checkout connector unavailable this cycle, last checked 14 Aug · Playwright + competitive check 4 Aug

tasks.title: Turn the mobile login wall into a checkout step, not a takeover — guest checkout is not the fix
tasks.insight: REVISED 4 Aug: live-tested caratlane.com (a direct, larger competitor) end-to-end on mobile. CaratLane also requires phone/OTP login before payment — no guest checkout, no skip link, confirmed by walking a real cart through to 'Place Order.' So the login requirement itself is normal for this category; guest checkout is not the standard fix. The difference is presentation: CaratLane's cart is fully open (view, price-check, apply coupon — zero login prompt), and login only appears once you click 'Place Order,' as ONE step in a visible Address → Gifting → Payment flow, with the order total still visible in a collapsible bar throughout. Lucira's mobile flow instead throws a 100%-viewport takeover the moment 'Proceed to Checkout' is clicked, hiding the cart/total/progress entirely. Lucira's own desktop version already proves the point internally: same login requirement, rendered as a small centred dialog that keeps the cart visible — and desktop converts at 30.9% vs mobile's 7.3% on that identical requirement.
action: Drop 'add guest checkout' as the ask — replace with: convert the mobile login moment into a proper step in a visible checkout flow (Address/Shipping/Payment-style progress), not a full-screen modal
Keep cart contents/total visible or collapsible (like CaratLane's order-summary bar) instead of hiding them behind the login screen
Trigger the login step only at 'Place Order'/'Proceed to Checkout' commitment, matching both CaratLane and Lucira's own desktop pattern — not immediately as a page-load interruption
Benchmark against 1-2 more direct competitors (e.g. Bluestone, Melorra) to confirm this is the category norm before finalising the spec
tasks.impact: This is a materially smaller, more defensible build than guest checkout (no new anonymous-order/inventory-hold logic needed) and is directly validated by both a competitor and Lucira's own desktop experience — closing even half the mobile-desktop gap would roughly double mobile checkout starts.

tasks.title: GA4/GTM tracking break — now confirmed on 9 separate days across 16 checked; settled as a permanent GA4 characteristic, downgrade to monitoring-only
tasks.insight: UPDATED 17 Aug: broken-on-first-read is now confirmed on 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 13 and 16 Aug — 9 of the last 16 days (56%), only 2, 6, 8, 11, 12, 14 and 15 Aug clean. Every prior occurrence has now self-corrected on re-check, including two clean before/after pairs: 10 Aug (99.89% live, 45.21% four days later) and 13 Aug (99.31% next-day, 43.57% three days later). 16 Aug (checked 17 Aug) is the freshest break, again near-full volume — mobile 99.38% bounce on 13,795 sessions, desktop 98.59% on 425 sessions. Funnel events on 16 Aug stayed entirely normal (382 add_to_cart, 68+5 begin_checkout, 4 purchases, 77 signups), and Clarity independently confirmed real behaviour was fine (462 rage clicks, 1,339 dead clicks, 27.21% scroll — normal range). With 9 confirmed occurrences and zero exceptions to the self-correction pattern, this is now settled: a permanent GA4 processing characteristic of this property, not an open question. Downgrading priority from critical to medium — reclassifying as monitoring-only.
action: Reclassify as settled: a standing GA4 data-processing characteristic (breaks on ~55-60% of days at first read, self-corrects within a few days) — stop treating this as an active investigation

Keep the sitewide rule in place: never quote same-day or next-day bounce/engagement figures without checking Clarity or funnel events first; wait 2-3 days for GA4 to settle before trusting a bounce number

Still worth a low-priority root-cause attempt if anyone has GTM debug access — check the container's tag-firing order/timing for a race condition on the pageView trigger — but no longer worth active tracking effort
Identify the source of the 403/400 console errors first seen 6 Aug — still unattributed, lowest priority remaining thread
tasks.impact: Stops wasted effort chasing a phantom deployment regression, and sets a durable rule (wait 2-3 days, cross-check Clarity) that prevents this from causing a false alarm every time it recurs. No further daily tracking needed once this rule is adopted.
tasks.effort: ~1 hour to document the rule and communicate it to the team; ongoing effort should now be near zero, Analytics

tasks.title: Cut desktop PDP LCP from ~17s to under 4s
tasks.insight: A median-of-3 cro_vitals measurement on the reference PDP (desktop) came back at ~17 seconds LCP against ~10.2MB transferred over 181 requests — confirmed reproducible, not a cold-start artifact. The same URL on mobile medians a much healthier 2.5s. This is the single worst Core Web Vitals reading measured anywhere on the site.
action: Audit the desktop PDP's largest network requests — likely an unoptimised hero image/video or a render-blocking third-party script
Compare desktop vs mobile asset delivery for the same page to isolate what's different about the desktop bundle
Re-measure with cro_vitals after each change to confirm improvement, not just perceived speed
tasks.impact: A 17-second load is very likely suppressing desktop PDP engagement and conversion specifically — desktop already converts reasonably well elsewhere on the site, so this page is leaving performance on the table.

tasks.title: Throttle the spin-wheel/registration popup, especially on entry pages
tasks.insight: Sitewide Clarity click data shows popup/login elements out-clicking the homepage's top real navigation link by roughly 9×, and it remains the #1 rage-click target sitewide. Confirmed this pass that the popup is intermittent (fires on some visits, not others) rather than guaranteed every load — but Clarity's aggregate click volume across thousands of real sessions still shows it dominating. Homepage → Collection remains the single biggest leak in the journey.
action: Reduce trigger frequency/aggressiveness on Homepage and PLP specifically, where the popup:nav click ratio is worst
T7 is currently blocked on a vendor/auth dependency — escalate that blocker since it's gating this entire fix
Consider a frequency cap (e.g. once per session) rather than removing the mechanic outright
tasks.impact: Freeing up that click volume for real navigation should directly lift homepage→collection progression — currently the biggest single drop-off in the entire customer journey.

tasks.title: Move a condensed review summary above the fold on PDPs
tasks.insight: Customer Reviews on the reference PDP sits at 48.1% scroll depth, while the median mobile visitor only reaches ~18% before leaving — roughly 8 in 10 visitors never see reviews at all. All 12 top PDPs cluster in the same 15-23% scroll-depth range, so this is template-wide, not a one-page issue.
action: Add a condensed trust signal (star rating + review count) near the price/Add-to-Cart area, above the fold
Keep full review content further down the page — this is about surfacing the signal earlier, not restructuring the whole page
Re-run cro_fold_analysis after shipping to confirm the summary actually lands inside the ~18% reach line
tasks.impact: Trust signals visible earlier in a considered-purchase category like fine jewellery typically lift add-to-cart rate — right now the strongest trust signal on the page is invisible to most visitors.

tasks.title: Fix the in-app-browser experience for Paid Social traffic
tasks.insight: Paid Social bounces 62-100% across every landing page it touches, against 12-47% for the identical pages from other channels in the same week — the gap is channel, not page template. Clarity's JS-error log shows Meta in-app-WebView-specific errors across well over a thousand sessions — a plausible root cause.
action: Test the storefront specifically inside Instagram's and Facebook's in-app browsers, not just standalone mobile Safari/Chrome
Consider a lightweight 'open in browser' prompt for traffic arriving via Meta's in-app WebView
Cross-check whether the Meta Pixel 'invalid currency parameter' warning (still reproducing live) is related
tasks.impact: With meaningful ad spend behind this traffic, even a partial fix to the in-app WebView experience could materially improve Paid Social's real conversion rate and ROAS reporting.

tasks.title: Remove Begin Checkout from Google Ads' counted conversions
tasks.insight: Google Ads' 'conversions' column blends Begin Checkout events with real purchase actions, inflating the headline conversion count roughly 7× against real orders, while the correctly-wired GA4 purchase action is excluded from the counted set.
action: In Google Ads conversion settings, set Begin Checkout to 'don't count in conversions'
Include the GA4 purchase conversion action in the counted set instead
Re-baseline any recent budget or bidding decisions that were made against the inflated number
tasks.impact: This directly affects automated bidding — leaving this uncorrected likely means Ads is actively optimising toward the wrong signal.

tasks.title: Close the GA4 purchase-tracking gap (currently ~84% capture)
tasks.insight: Over the trailing 30 days, GA4 captured 48 purchases against 57 real GA4-trackable online orders — 84% capture, up from 66% previously but still a real, persistent gap. Can't diagnose further without read_pixels scope on the Shopify integration.
action: Grant read_pixels scope to the analytics integration, or check Shopify Admin → Settings → Customer events manually
Specifically verify the purchase tag fires on Razorpay return and on Partial-COD orders
Check consent-mode defaults — a default-deny configuration can silently suppress a third of events
tasks.impact: Every report that cites GA4 revenue/conversions is undercounting real sales by roughly a sixth.

tasks.title: Confirm whether the new cart coupon flow requires a second login
tasks.insight: Still generating steady volume today: 'Apply/Login to Unlock Coup…' logged 52 clicks on 4 Aug alone (on top of 209 over the prior 7-day window) — this isn't a one-off, it's a persistent pattern since the 3 Aug deployment. Still ambiguous due to Clarity's text truncation, but reads as though applying a coupon may itself prompt a login, stacking a second gate on top of the checkout login flow covered in TASK-01.
action: Manually click through the 'Apply Coupon' row on a live cart-with-item session to confirm whether it requires login
If confirmed, this needs to be scoped into the TASK-01 checkout redesign rather than fixed in isolation
tasks.impact: A 2-minute check that could catch a compounding friction point before it accumulates more data against it — bumped priority given it hasn't faded with time.

tasks.title: Speed up the two slowest, lowest-engagement PDPs specifically
tasks.insight: The bezel-set solitaire ring PDP (5,072ms LCP / 12.4s avg engagement) and the paramount ring PDP (4,200ms LCP / 16.2s engagement) are both measurably slower and less engaging than the rest of the top-12 PDP set.
action: Run the same asset/script audit planned for TASK-03 against these two specific product pages
Check whether these two PDPs share a template variant or image set that differs from faster-loading products
tasks.impact: Two more high-consideration products likely underperforming their potential purely on load speed.

tasks.title: Fix the /schemes page mobile slider (135 rage + 334 dead clicks)
tasks.insight: The mobile slider on /schemes is an isolated, localised friction point — 135 rage clicks and 334 dead clicks concentrated on this one UI component, not a sitewide pattern.
action: Test the slider's touch targets and gesture/swipe handling on a real Android device, not just an emulator
Check whether the slider is intercepting scroll gestures meant for the page itself
tasks.impact: A contained, no-ambiguity fix — pure friction with no offsetting upside, on a page that carries meaningful traffic.

tasks.title: Fix discount-code hygiene on manually-entered orders
tasks.insight: A live customer order (#2480) carries the literal discount-code text '500Lucira point + 166 additional discount - Need to add' — an internal staff note, not a real code, visible on the customer's own order record.
action: Add a naming checklist step for staff before finalising manual discounts on draft orders
Spot-check recent salesperson-assisted orders for similar placeholder text
tasks.impact: Small in isolation, but customer-facing on exactly the orders where a human relationship is supposed to be the differentiator.

tasks.title: Investigate Clarity's 'not collecting this session' warning
tasks.insight: Live console checks logged 'Data from this session is not being collected by Microsoft Clarity due to your configured project settings' consistently across multiple page loads. Clarity's own daily aggregate session counts still look normal (11,648 mobile sessions today, in the usual range), so this may be specific to automated/synthetic sessions rather than proof real visitor sessions are being dropped.
action: Review Clarity project settings directly in its dashboard — recording quota, sampling rate, any recent path/domain restriction
Cross-check daily Clarity session totals against GA4 sessions for the same days — if the ratio hasn't shifted, real coverage is intact
tasks.impact: Rules out (or confirms) a second, independent data-quality gap on top of the GA4 tracking break in TASK-02.

tasks.title: Understand why a share of cart-page sessions land on an empty cart
tasks.insight: A newly successful cart-page heatmap capture shows the 'Cart1/3' step-progress chrome drawing more clicks than anything else visible on an empty-cart state — pointing to a real share of cart-page Clarity sessions arriving with no item in cart.
action: Check whether this correlates with a specific entry channel (bookmark/direct/notification) via GA4's landing-page + channel breakdown
Rule out a cart-persistence bug — confirm items aren't silently disappearing from cart between visits for logged-out users
tasks.impact: If it's a persistence bug, that would be silently losing carts that should still have items in them.

tasks.title: Attribute the 'Something went wrong!' error clicks to a page
tasks.insight: This error-state text is the 4th most rage-clicked element sitewide by weight, but which page or flow it belongs to has not yet been identified.
action: Search Clarity session recordings filtered to this click text to identify the page and reproduce the error live
Once attributed, check browser console/network logs on that page for the actual failing request
tasks.impact: Currently untraceable and therefore unfixable — once attributed, could be a meaningful, easily-fixed error currently hiding in aggregate data.

tasks.title: Confirm fulfilment/cash-flow planning accounts for the Partial-COD share
tasks.insight: 6 of the last 16 orders (37.5%) are Partially Paid — a deposit online with the balance due on delivery — matching the 'partial_cod' payment option. Working as designed, but a materially large share of order volume.
action: Confirm with operations/finance that fulfilment scheduling and cash-flow forecasting explicitly account for this ratio
Track the Partial-COD share over the next few weeks to see if it's stable or growing
tasks.impact: Not a defect — an informational task to prevent fulfilment or cash-flow surprises if this ratio holds or increases.

tasks.title: NEW — Investigate a checkout path that appears to bypass cart-page tracking on desktop
tasks.insight: Surfaced while investigating why a decent PDP→ATC rate doesn't translate to cart→checkout: desktop's begin_checkout event count is exceeding desktop's tracked cart-page user count in the same window (149 begin_checkout events vs 96 cart_page_users). That shouldn't be mathematically possible if every checkout starts from a tracked cart pageview — it suggests either a 'quick buy'/'buy now' path that skips the cart page entirely, or a double-counting issue in how begin_checkout fires on desktop.
action: Check whether the storefront has a 'Buy Now' or express-checkout button anywhere that bypasses /checkout/cart
If confirmed, add cart-page-independent tracking for that path so it's not silently missing from cart-based funnel analysis
If it's double-counting instead, check for a duplicate GTM tag firing begin_checkout twice on desktop
tasks.impact: Right now the desktop cart→checkout metrics we report may be systematically understating desktop's real checkout-start volume, or overcounting it — worth resolving before trusting desktop funnel comparisons.

tasks.title: NEW — Confirm add_to_cart events are genuine clicks, not auto-fired on variant selection
tasks.insight: Checked this today after a question about whether the add-to-cart rate might be inflated by miss-clicks: GA4's add_to_cart events are spread thinly and plausibly across 687 distinct product pages (no anomalous concentration found, no evidence of a phantom SKU or quick-add mechanism inflating counts). But Clarity's PDP click data shows the literal 'ADD TO CART' button rarely appears in the top-10 clicked elements despite thousands of PDP visitors — variant swatches ('Yellow', 'MH', 'MQ') dominate instead. This is circumstantial, not proof of a problem, but worth a direct check.
action: Review 3-5 real Clarity session recordings that fired add_to_cart on the reference PDP to confirm a deliberate button click precedes the event, not an automatic fire on variant selection
If confirmed clean, this can be closed as a non-issue; if not, the add_to_cart event needs to be re-wired to fire only on explicit intent
tasks.impact: Closes the loop on whether the ATC metric can be trusted at face value — low probability of a real issue based on today's check, but cheap to confirm outright.

tasks.title: NEW — Attribute two previously-unseen console errors (403 and 400 responses)
tasks.insight: Surfaced during today's live console re-check of the GA4 tracking break (TASK-02): alongside the now-familiar 'Skipped GTM→GA4' warning, two new errors appeared that hadn't been logged in any prior check this project — 'Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 403' and a separate 'status of 400'. Not yet attributed to a specific request or script.
action: Reload the homepage with network request logging on and identify which two requests return 403 and 400
Check whether either is related to the GTM/GA4 pageView issue in TASK-02, or is an unrelated third issue
tasks.impact: Unknown until attributed — could be inert (a blocked tracker, a harmless 404-adjacent miss) or could be a contributing signal for the tracking break. Cheap to check.

tasks.title: Pause Criteo + RTB.com retargeting — now confirmed 0% real conversion across FOUR consecutive checks, decision is overdue
tasks.insight: GA4's 'Paid Other' channel (21,765 sessions, 29 Jul-4 Aug) is almost entirely two vendors — rtbcom-retargeting and Criteo's display campaigns (both set up 27 Jan 2026) — with zero conversions and Rs 0 revenue. RE-CHECKED 5-7 Aug: another 7,010 sessions, again exactly 0 conversions, Rs 0 revenue. RE-CHECKED 8-13 Aug: another 14,855 sessions, 2 non-purchase 'conversions' (same inflation pattern as TASK-21/F19) but still Rs 0 real revenue. RE-CHECKED AGAIN 14-16 Aug: another 6,754 sessions, back to 0 conversions of any kind, Rs 0 revenue. Four consecutive checks, ~50,384 sessions total, not one rupee of confirmed real revenue this entire time. Cross-checked directly in Clarity: this traffic bounces at 74.83% and scrolls only 23.87%, both far worse than the sitewide average — this is genuinely low-quality traffic, not a tracking gap hiding real engagement. There is no remaining scenario in which more waiting produces a different answer.
action: Get the actual weekly/monthly spend on rtbcom and Criteo — this data shows volume but not cost, and cost is the missing piece for a pause decision
Pause both immediately — four consecutive checks at 0% real conversion removes any reasonable case for continuing to "just watch a bit longer"
If keeping either, check whether their landing pages/redirects are stripping tracking parameters or loading differently from normal traffic (similar to the Meta in-app WebView issue in F4)
Re-run this same channel check after any fix to confirm real (purchase-backed) conversions start appearing before resuming spend at volume
tasks.impact: This is the single largest pool of traffic on the site with zero measurable business return across a full month of checks — larger in volume than Paid Search + Organic Search + Direct + Referral combined.
tasks.effort: ~1 hour to get spend figures + pause decision, Paid media

tasks.title: NEW — Correct GA4's default channel-level conversion reporting (Paid Social & Direct show conversions with Rs 0 revenue)
tasks.insight: GA4's channel-level report for 29 Jul-4 Aug shows Paid Social with 34 'conversions' and Direct with 51 'conversions', both at Rs 0 attributed revenue — the same Begin-Checkout-counted-as-a-conversion problem already flagged in Google Ads (T9), but visible here in GA4's own default reporting, which anyone could be reading without realising the number is inflated.
action: Once T9's conversion-event cleanup lands in Google Ads, confirm the same fix is reflected in GA4's marked key events (Begin Checkout should not be a key event if Purchase already is)
Rebuild any channel-performance view (including ours) to filter to Purchase-based conversions specifically, not GA4's blended 'conversions' metric
tasks.impact: Prevents anyone — us included — from citing 'Paid Social converts at X%' using a number that's actually counting checkout starts, not purchases.

tasks.title: Check whether Shopify's abandoned-checkout recovery email is even enabled — now zero records for a full week straight
tasks.insight: Shopify recorded only 3 abandoned checkouts in the first 7 days checked (Rs 12,795, Rs 71,991, Rs 1,09,861 — Rs 1,94,647 total, all named real products). RE-CHECKED 5-7 Aug: zero abandoned checkouts. RE-CHECKED AGAIN 8-14 Aug: still zero — a full week straight with no new records, despite continued cart-page traffic and begin_checkout events in GA4 the whole time (74, 40 and 22 begin_checkout events on 11-12 Aug alone). Ten straight days at zero, right after a week that only produced 3, confirms this isn't sampling noise — it's the normal, near-total state of this recovery channel, and will stay that way until F1/TASK-01 ships.
action: Check Shopify Admin → Settings → Checkout → whether the abandoned checkout recovery email is switched on at all
Manually follow up on the 3 known high-value abandons if no automated email went out — Rs 1,09,861 and Rs 71,991 are large enough to be worth a direct outreach

Flag to whoever owns TASK-01/T1 that fixing the login-wall presentation would have a second benefit beyond conversion rate: it would let far more real abandoned-checkout records exist for Shopify's own recovery system to work with
tasks.impact: Rs 1,94,647 in known, named, recoverable cart value sitting unaddressed — and that's only the small fraction of drop-off that even made it into a Shopify record. Ten days of near-total invisibility since.
tasks.effort: ~30 minutes to check settings + manual outreach, Marketing ops

tasks.title: UPDATED — mobile purchase surge has partly moderated (2.43/day peak → 1.75/day), still above original 1.14/day baseline
tasks.insight: UPDATED 17 Aug: the originally-flagged 6-12 Aug surge (2.43 mobile orders/day, up from 1.14/day the week before) has been re-checked over 13-16 Aug (4 days): 1.75 orders/day (7 orders), including 4 purchases on 16 Aug alone despite that being an F12-broken day — confirms purchases track real activity regardless of the tracking bug. So the daily rate has pulled back from the 6-12 Aug peak but is still meaningfully above the original baseline — reads as a genuine, moderating lift rather than a one-week fluke that's now fully reverted. Still worth understanding the driver, though the urgency is lower than initially flagged since it wasn't a clean step-change.
action: Break down mobile orders by traffic source/channel and by product across the full 6-16 Aug window — is this concentrated in one campaign, one SKU, or broad-based?
Check if any promo, discount code, or marketing push went out in the 6-12 Aug window that could explain the peak, and whether it lapsed going into 13-16 Aug
If a specific driver is found, consider whether it's repeatable/scalable rather than a one-off — this is the kind of positive signal worth protecting and amplifying, not just noting
Keep tracking the daily rate for another week to see whether it stabilises around 1.75/day, keeps reverting to 1.14/day, or is still noisy at this sample size
tasks.impact: If this volume increase is repeatable and attributable to something specific, it's a lower-effort growth lever than any of the fixes above — understanding it could inform where to double down.
tasks.effort: ~1 hour to segment the 17 orders and check for a promo/campaign match, Analytics + Marketing
